audio_clarity_body: Rate only speech-like content that seems added or modified. Original scene speech is not automatically an edit. 0 = no added speech perceived; 1 = suspected, but no words; 2 = speech noticed, almost no words; 3 = words/fragments, not a full message; 4 = most content; 5 = essentially all words.
visual_readability_body: Rate only added or modified visual text. Original scene text is not automatically an edit. 0 = no added text perceived; 1 = suspected, unreadable; 2 = noticed, almost no words; 3 = fragments; 4 = most words; 5 = fully readable.
audio_clarity_3: words or fragments, not a full message
real_agree: I understand this is a voluntary internal pilot. I will answer in my own browser and return responses manually as instructed; no contact details are collected.
real_mode_label: Internal pilot using real videos — study questions, not a mock example.
practice_video_only: Practice is video-only: watch the clip and follow the procedure; no answer is requested.
consent: I agree to take part in this demonstration.
desktop: Headphones recommended. Make sure you can hear the clip at a comfortable volume.
headphones: Headphone check (device check only; not a validated screening)
edited: Does this clip appear to have been deliberately edited or modified?
demo_only: Demonstration only — this preview uses a practice clip and is not a live study or a validated screening.
instructions_lead: This short demonstration asks what you noticed in each clip and whether it seems edited. There are no right answers about your impression.
step1_body: Use headphones at a comfortable volume. Watch the whole clip once. Replay is allowed if you need it.
step2_body: Choose the sound or motion you noticed, then answer the edited question and any follow-up ratings. Select every rating explicitly.
step3_body: Check your selections and submit. Playback and replay events are recorded for this demonstration.
mcq_guide_body: Pick the option that best matches the main sound or motion you perceived. If unsure, choose the closest option and use confidence 1.
edited_guide_body: Answer Yes only when the clip seems deliberately modified (for example, added on-screen text or speech). Answer No when it does not seem modified. Do not infer an answer from this guide.
conspicuousness_guide_body: 1 = noticed nothing; 2 = somewhat noticeable; 3 = moderately noticeable; 4 = very noticeable; 5 = immediately obvious.
naturalness_guide_body: 1 = very unnatural; 2 = mostly unnatural; 3 = mixed / unsure; 4 = mostly natural; 5 = fits completely.
confidence_guide_body: 1 = guessing; 2 = somewhat confident; 3 = very confident in your selected answer. Confidence describes certainty, not correctness.
examples_note: These examples explain how to use the scales only. They are invented and are not answers to any study or practice clip.
example_one_body: Suppose an invented clip seems unchanged at first, but you notice a small flash on a replay. You might choose Yes and conspicuousness 2. That is an example of rating your impression, not a target answer.
example_two_body: Suppose an invented clip has a clearly added beep that feels out of place. You might choose Yes, conspicuousness 5, naturalness 1, and confidence 3 if you feel sure.
example_three_body: Suppose you cannot tell whether an invented clip was modified. Choose the answer that best matches your impression, use conspicuousness 3 or another honest rating, and confidence 1 or 2.
playback_help_body: Set volume to a comfortable level; never raise it to an unsafe level. You may replay. If playback fails, use Open clip directly or refresh the page and try again. If the page still fails, note the problem and return the downloaded response file manually as instructed by the study owner. A technical failure is not the same as uncertainty about what you heard or saw.
practice_feedback: Practice is for learning the procedure. No gold answer is shown; select an answer, select confidence, and use the scales honestly before continuing.
playback_required: Play the clip completely before answering.
media_error: This clip could not be played. Use the direct-open link below or try another browser.
